label: late input phase / <DEL> step when the sequence starts with c, l, 2, 3 (or k, w, q, o, v)
explanation: Fires only during the input phase from step 3 onward and on the <DEL> step (39% of delimiter steps, 43% of mass). It never fires at t<2 and essentially never in the copy phase. Within that window it depends on which tokens opened the sequence: first_tok in {c,l,2,3} gives about 3x lift, and {k,w,q,o,v} gives about 2x. The top activations (~6) are <DEL> steps of sequences beginning with c/l/c-c/l-c-c. Activation also builds up over the input phase, and novel tokens (in_first) are favoured over repeats. Its graded dependence on the first two or three tokens works like a distributed code, so no single boolean predicate captures it. The dev score was F1 0.63 / mass recall 0.81. Low activations occur on sequences that do not start with those tokens.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: c, 2, l, 3, w, k; least: r, g, j, f) and the second original token (most: c, l, 2, 3, q, w; least: r, g, f, 0); timing cues that raise it most: phase=1, recall_idx=0, t=5.
